criteria.criterion: A clone on a stale epoch reaching sync._union_merge returns without merging and preserves both pre-operation refs exactly.
A clone on a stale epoch reaching push.py's non-FF retry returns without merging or re-pushing and preserves both pre-operation refs exactly.
Assert on the emitted log record (caplog), plus one subprocess run with REBAR_SYNC_PUSH=always proving the message reaches a real operator's stderr.
At the push.py site the retry loop terminates immediately on epoch mismatch: exactly zero merge invocations and zero further push attempts, and the push remains not-completed.
After a guard-aborted non-fast-forward push, fsck reports DIVERGED and does not report PUSH_PENDING; local and remote tips remain byte-for-byte unchanged.
At the sync._union_merge site the function returns without merging and the clone is left un-converged (not corrupted).
A merely-behind clone (matching epochs) still converges via ff-adopt, and a strictly-ahead clone still returns early — neither is blocked.
Every row of the state matrix is asserted, including the two distinct absences (record-absent vs record-present-epoch-absent) and the corrupt-record row.
git show failing because the ref is unreadable produces a different message than the file being absent at a readable ref.
An older binary reading a record that carries epoch does not error and does not fail closed. Tier: unit against compat._analyze.
write_compat_record preserves an existing valid string epoch, leaves a pre-epoch record absent, and never generates a new epoch value.
The remote side is read via git show <remote_ref>:.store-compat.json, not the local worktree.
